question: Why does knowing a little about a subject make you more curious about it than knowing nothing at all?
answer: Because curiosity needs a visible gap. Loewenstein argued that it is triggered when attention falls on a gap between what one knows and what one wants to know. Knowing nothing, there is no gap to notice; knowing some, the missing piece stands out. A crossword with three clues left nags more than a blank one.
move: To feel curious, learn just enough to see what is missing.
ask: Which subject do I find dull only because I know too little about it to see the gaps?
reference: Loewenstein, The psychology of curiosity: A review and reinterpretation, Psychological Bulletin, 1994
